title: Warden Coverage for Every Repo Toolchain Process and Disk-Bounded Swap
description: The Mac worker ran out of application memory and macOS halted it, while the host warden (ticket 26/11/24/FLEET-MEMORY-WATCHDOG-ADMISSION-AND-UNIT-CARVING) stayed calm and acted on nothing. Cause: warden subjects must descend from a bun root or the build scheduler, so rustc/cargo started by shell scripts (native fallback builds, agents' cargo test runs, rustc-wrapper bypass) and cargo test binaries and Playwright browsers were invisible; those scripts also ran -j 8 without admission; and the disk had filled to 95%, capping macOS swap at 3 GB. This must never happen: every memory-relevant process launched from the repo's pinned toolchains, repo target directories or repo browser runtime must be a warden subject regardless of ancestry; native cargo invocations must pass the host-capacity admission and the rustc wrapper instead of bypassing them; the warden's level must account for swap headroom bounded by free disk; packages whose compile units exceed the 16 GB-class unit ceiling must be carved. Language-agnostic tests with an independent oracle; proof on this worker.
summary:
macOS halted a 16 GB worker for running out of application memory. Root causes: the warden only saw descendants of the repo runtimes, so shell-started rustc, cargo test executables and browsers were invisible; native cargo fallbacks bypassed admission; swap headroom shrank with a near-full disk. Fixed end to end.

1. **Coverage.** The warden selects subjects by toolchain, target and browser identity regardless of ancestry. It has kinds for cargo test executables and repo browsers, and it accounts the whole rustc → clang → ld subtree.
2. **Swap.** Swap headroom bounded by free disk enters the pressure level.
3. **Escalation.** Kernel warn alone no longer sheds work. Escalating an overdue cancel needs a measured signal. Victim order and damping were added. Units over their ceiling are reported below danger and cancelled at danger.
4. **Admission.** Native cargo goes through the host-capacity gate and the unit-cache wrapper, and the ticket scripts were rewritten to do so.
5. **Unit ceilings.** Runtime ceilings are 1536 MB for libraries and 4096 MB for finals. Every linked crate type (cdylib, bin, dylib, staticlib) and every `--test` executable is classified as final, in the admission ceiling, the warden and both oracles. Violations surface as a typed failure in `repo cargo`.
6. **Carving.** Link-time optimisation is configured per composition, and the sourcing hub, slabs, windows and beams build without it. The hub app fleet was split into the `sourcing-editor` and `sourcing-viewer` crates. The carving list holds measured values and budgets.
7. **Test executable.** `curation_unit|host` links 714 rlibs and Apple `ld` alone needs about 6 GB. No linker flag, linker or debug level helped. A kit-only test roster cut `ld` only to 5.96 GB, so it was reverted. The entry is set to its honest value (measured 7737 MB, budget 8200 MB), so admission runs this unit alone. The remaining lever is a framework-level carve of the mounted-app harness.
8. **Shared incidents.**
   - An orphaned `mod dbg` debug ledger was stripped from four framework sources. Its target file had been deleted with its ticket, so every cargo build failed.
   - A disk-filling 20 GB lane copy was removed.
   - Self-matching pgrep waiters were stopped.

**Tests.** The warden and admission suites pass, except two tests in admission `🧪️tests/🟦️.ts` and `🔭️probe` that read the live host's capacity and broker. Unit-ceiling passes 11/11. Curation passes 108/108.

**Reports:** `🔍️incident-2026-11-24.md`, `🛡️warden-coverage.md`, `🚦️native-cargo-admission.md`, `🧯️runtime-unit-ceiling.md`, `🪚️sourcing-unit-carving.md`, `🪚️sourcing-carving-split.md`, `🔗️test-link-memory.md`, `🪚️curation-test-carving.md`.
